1.outline: Term theme: 'Analyse, Present & Code'. Bring together this year's spreadsheet toolkit — SUM, AVERAGE, IF and a lookup — on a real dataset.
1.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, sample dataset.
objectives: Apply SUM, AVERAGE, IF and a lookup to a dataset.
Choose the right function for a given question.
Check results are sensible against the raw data.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Apply the toolkit
plan.detail: On a real dataset (e.g. sports results or survey data), apply SUM, AVERAGE, IF and a lookup to answer given questions.

plan.title: Sanity check
plan.detail: Check two results manually against the raw data to catch formula mistakes.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

activities: Apply four functions to real data
successCriteria: I applied SUM, AVERAGE, IF and a lookup correctly.
I chose the right function for each question.
I checked my results made sense.

2.outline: Choose the chart type that best makes an analytical point — not just any chart, but the one that answers the question.
2.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, chart-choice poster.
objectives: State the analytical question a chart should answer.
Choose the chart type that best answers it.
Justify the choice against an alternative.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Question first
plan.detail: Given a question (e.g. 'has this trend changed over time?'), decide the chart type before building it.

plan.title: Build and compare
plan.detail: Build the chosen chart, then build an alternative type and compare which answers the question better.

plan.title: Justify
plan.detail: Write one sentence justifying the final choice. Save and log out.

activities: Build and compare two chart types
successCriteria: I chose a chart type based on the question, not habit.
I compared it against an alternative.
I justified my final choice.

3.outline: Build a small analysis dashboard combining formulas and charts that together answer a real question about the dataset.
3.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, dashboard exemplar.
objectives: Combine formulas and charts into one analysis.
Arrange them so the analysis is easy to follow.
Check the dashboard actually answers the chosen question.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Build the dashboard
plan.detail: Combine key formulas and one or two charts into a single, clearly arranged view.

plan.title: Question check
plan.detail: Check the dashboard actually answers the analytical question chosen this week.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

successCriteria: My dashboard combines formulas and at least one chart.
My dashboard is clearly arranged.
My dashboard answers the chosen analytical question.

4.outline: Design a presentation deck to communicate the analysis findings, applying strong slide-design principles.
4.sowResources: Microsoft PowerPoint, Google Slides, design principles handout.
objectives: Apply strong slide-design principles.
Build a deck that communicates the analysis clearly.
Include the dashboard chart in the deck.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Design principles recap
plan.detail: Recap one idea per slide, minimal text, consistent theme.

plan.title: Build the deck
plan.detail: Build a 4-5 slide deck: title, context, findings with the chart, conclusion.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

successCriteria: My deck follows strong design principles.
My deck clearly communicates the analysis.
My deck includes the dashboard chart.

5.outline: Revisit core Python from Year 7-8: input/output, variables, if/elif/else, loops — ready to build a small tool.
objectives: Recall input, output, variables and conditions.
Recall for and while loops.
Write a short program using several of these together.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Rapid recap
plan.detail: Quickfire recap: input/output, variables, if/elif/else, loops — one example of each.

plan.title: Combine them
plan.detail: Write a short program combining at least three of these concepts.

plan.title: Test it
plan.detail: Test the program with a partner. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I recalled the core Python concepts correctly.
My program combines at least three of them.
My program was tested and works.

6.outline: Build a small, genuinely useful Python tool — for example a grade calculator, a simple quiz, or a unit converter.
objectives: Plan a small useful Python tool.
Build it using variables, conditions and/or loops.
Test it with realistic use.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Choose a tool
plan.detail: Choose a small tool idea and plan its inputs and outputs.

plan.title: Build it
plan.detail: Build the tool using this term's Python skills.

plan.title: Test it
plan.detail: Test it as a real user would. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I planned a small useful tool.
My tool works using variables and conditions/loops.
I tested it as a real user would.

7.outline: Present the data analysis deck to the class, and briefly demo the Python tool.
objectives: Present the analysis findings clearly.
Demo the Python tool briefly.
Answer one question about either piece of work.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Present findings
plan.detail: Present the analysis deck, timed, to a small group or the class.

plan.title: Demo the tool
plan.detail: Briefly demo the Python tool running live.

plan.title: Questions
plan.detail: Answer one audience question about either piece of work. Log out.

successCriteria: I presented my analysis findings clearly and within time.
I demoed my Python tool live.
I answered a question about my work.

8.outline: Curate this term's work into the portfolio: the analysis dashboard, the presentation deck, and the Python tool.
objectives: Gather this term's finished work into one place.
Check all three pieces are complete and correctly named.
Save everything to the portfolio folder.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Gather and check
plan.detail: Collect the dashboard, deck and Python tool; check each is finished and correctly named.

plan.title: Portfolio save
plan.detail: Save all three into the term portfolio folder.

plan.title: Log out
plan.detail: Log out.

successCriteria: All three pieces of work are gathered together.
Each piece is finished and correctly named.
Everything is saved in the portfolio folder.

9.outline: Choose one piece of work — dashboard, deck or Python tool — and add one polish feature to it.
9.sowResources: Microsoft Excel / Google Sheets, Thonny, Microsoft PowerPoint / Google Slides.
objectives: Choose one piece of work to improve.
Add one meaningful polish feature.
Re-check the piece still works correctly.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Add polish
plan.detail: Choose and improve one piece of work with a meaningful addition.

plan.title: Re-check
plan.detail: Re-check the piece still works correctly after the change.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

successCriteria: I chose one piece of work to improve.
I added a meaningful polish feature.
The piece still works correctly.

10.outline: Rehearse the term's full skill set in pairs: analysis formula, chart choice, deck design, Python basics.
10.sowResources: Recap slide deck, practice task cards.
objectives: Recall the term's full skill set.
Rehearse an analysis-to-presentation task with a partner.
Identify the trickiest step.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Skill recap
plan.detail: Recap: analyse, chart, present, code — as a class chant.

plan.title: Paired rehearsal
plan.detail: Practise a mini analysis-to-slide task with a partner reading the task card, then swap.

plan.title: Tricky step check
plan.detail: Name the step you still find hardest. Log out.

successCriteria: I can list the term's skill set in order.
I rehearsed the practical task with a partner.
I know which step needs more practice.

11.outline: Individual task: analyse a dataset with functions and a chart, then present the findings clearly.
objectives: Analyse a dataset with functions.
Choose and build the right chart.
Present findings clearly.

plan.title: Settle and explain
plan.detail: Calm start — explain the task and rubric.

plan.title: Analyse and chart
plan.detail: Individual practical: apply functions to a dataset and build a suitable chart.

plan.title: Present findings
plan.detail: Give a short spoken summary of the findings to the teacher.

plan.title: Celebrate
plan.detail: Save and celebrate the term's progress. Log out.

successCriteria: My analysis uses the right functions correctly.
My chart suits the data and question.
I presented my findings clearly.
